newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government seeks to save law after defeat.
newsitem.headline: Italian government seeks to save law after defeat.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government said on Friday it had done a deal with the opposition to try to rush through a law on tenants' rights after a previous attempt ended in an embarrassing defeat in parliament.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the draft law, which will ensure tenants facing eviction at the end of their rental contracts win a six-month stay, was unlikely to face problems in parliament.

"It should get rapid approval since there is an agreement in principle about it with the opposition," Prodi told a news conference after a cabinet meeting. Centre-right opposition politicians had no immediate comment.
Prodi was narrowly defeated in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Wednesday when the assembly rejected similar legislation presented in the form of a cabinet decree law.

The defeat was doubly embarrassing for the government, appointed in May, since it has said it will defend less well-off Italians but appeared unable to muster enough of its own supporters to turn up for the vote.
Public Works Minister Antonio Di Pietro said some 400,000 Italians who had been served eviction orders by their landlords could benefit from passage of the law.
He said the government would ask parliament for it to be approved at parliamentary commission level, avoiding lengthier passage through the full assemblies of the two houses.
Many tenants in Italy face the threat of eviction at the end of their contracts, even though they have paid the full rent, from landlords seeking more lucrative uses and occupants.
